Auserene or Rosebud? An honest comparison from one of them
Is Rosebud worth it? How it compares with Auserene

faq.a: If you want one journal that does it all, yes. Auserene connects quick notes, an evening conversation, a meditation made from your day, memory you can read and edit, people and habit goals, and it keeps a free plan. Rosebud is the better pick for therapy-style guided journals or if you need Android or the web.

Not anymore. Rosebud retired its free plan on September 30, 2026, according to its help center, though its homepage still says it's free to use. Rosebud Bloom costs $12.99 a month or $107.99 a year in the US.

Yes, for Bloom subscribers. Rosebud's long-term memory recalls people, topics and how they relate, and Rosebud says it does better with topics than with specific dates. It doesn't state whether you can view or edit individual memories.

Rosebud doesn't list a meditation or breathing feature on its site, App Store listing or help center. Auserene writes a guided meditation from each day's conversation, has eight guided meditation journeys, and does haptic breathing on Apple Watch.

faq.q: What is a good Rosebud alternative for iPhone?
faq.a: Auserene, if you want your notes, conversation, meditation, memory, people and goals in one connected app on iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch. Day One with its Gold plan, if you want a long archive with AI added. Apple Journal, if you want something free with no AI chat. Our Rosebud alternatives guide compares nine.

informationGain: A disclosed head-to-head built only from Rosebud's own pages on November 19, 2026, including its free-plan retirement against a homepage that still says it's free, its admitted weakness with dates in long-term memory, its unpublished weekly usage limits and Thrive tiers, and the absence of any meditation feature, set against Auserene's readable memory and meditation made from your day.
